pair_1_iaaspaas_vs_beyondcorp.verdict: KEEP — genuine tension, but narrow scope
pair_1_iaaspaas_vs_beyondcorp.rationale: Claim A says general CSPs (AWS/Azure) can't enforce ZT policies. Claim B says Google BeyondCorp IS the most mature cloud ZT implementation. Real contradiction but scope-limited: it's 'most CSPs can't' vs 'one CSP can.'

pair_2_iot_vs_device_mgmt.rationale: IoT devices can't be centrally managed (closed systems), but UEM/MDM IS the backbone for standard IT. This is IoT as exception-to-the-rule, not a genuine contradiction. Consider changing to 'extends' or 'qualifies.'

pair_3_iot_vs_firmware.rationale: Claim A says IoT has unpatchable firmware. Claim B says patch management MUST cover firmware below OS. Direct logical incompatibility.

pair_4_nac_vs_ise.rationale: Claim A says 802.1x NAC is incompatible with ZT. Claim B says NAC (Cisco ISE) functions as single source of truth. But B describes a migration reality ('each medium has distinct rollout characteristics') — it may be describing the starting point to migrate FROM, not endorsing NAC as ZT-native. Graham needs to read B's full context.
